transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-07
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Lars (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Priya (Atlas CTO), Carlos (Platform Eng), Evelyn (SecOps), Tom (SRE)

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough focusing on tracing, error analysis, request logs ingestion, and debugging flows. Customer interested in how Redwood surfaces errors from model endpoints, correlates traces to request IDs, and retains logs for audits. Want to validate Dedicated/private deployment options, VPC/KMS controls, and run a short pilot for latency/cost benchmarks.

Topics covered:
- Live demo of Console: Traces, Error Analysis view, Request Logs, filtering, and sample debugging workflow
- How request IDs and KV cache/kv-cache traces are represented
- Retention, encryption (KMS/HSM), RBAC and audit logs for compliance
- Canary rollouts, automatic fallback to cheaper model variants, and tracing across fallbacks
- Ingestion formats for request logs and recommended sampling rates for production

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone good afternoon, thanks for joining. Priya, Carlos, Evelyn, Tom — thanks for making time. We thought we'd run through the Redwood Console tracing and error analysis flows, show how request logs surface, and then demo a short debugging scenario. Lars and Sofia will jump into the demo.
[00:18] Priya (Atlas): Thanks Maya, yeah we wanna see how your tracing ties to specific requests — we have strict audit requirements and our SecOps needs to be able to pull logs for any user request id within 24 hours.
[00:27] Lars (Redwood-SE): Perfect, we'll show that. Quick agenda: tracing overview, open the traces UI, walk through an error analysis, then request logs ingestion and some tips for debugging.
[00:40] Carlos (Atlas): Also can you show how this works across Dedicated vs Hosted — we need to know whether request logs stay in our VPC or go to Redwood-managed storage?
[00:48] Sofia (Redwood-SE): Yep we'll call that out — Hosted keeps logs in Redwood storage with customer-scoped controls, Dedicated and Private allow you to configure where logs are sent (VPC endpoints, S3 buckets in your account) and use KMS for encryption.
[00:58] Maya (Redwood): Cool, I'll hand it to Lars.
[01:05] Lars (Redwood-SE): Alright pulling up the Console. You can see the tracing tab here, top nav. I'm starting a live query for requests in the last 2 hours for model redwood-alpha-1-dev.
[01:20] Lars: The traces view shows spans for each internal step — request ingestion, routing, model execution, kv-cache hit/miss, and any fallback. Each span has duration and tags. For example you can see a 320ms spike in the model execution span.
[01:37] Tom (SRE): Quick q — how do you correlate an API request to a trace? We use request IDs and our sidecar injects a header x-atlas-request-id.
[01:45] Lars: Great question. We accept customer request IDs via headers — x-request-id, x-atlas-request-id, whatever you standardize. The Console shows a Request ID column and you can click to expand the full trace.
[01:58] Priya: Is the request ID immutable when you do fallback to another model variant? We need to trace the same external request across retries and fallbacks.
[02:08] Sofia: Yes the external request id is preserved across retry/fallbacks in the trace metadata, we add internal span ids but keep the original header so you can filter. Sometimes transcription there was like KV cache spelled K V cache in older docs but it's consistent in the UI.
[02:24] Lars: I'm going to filter for requests that returned 5xx responses and had a model fallback. Notice the filter syntax — status:5xx AND fallback:true.
[02:34] Lars: Here's one sample request id: atlas-req-20270207-1142. Click to open the timeline.
[02:42] [02:42] (UI pause)
[02:45] Lars: You can see an error event in the model execution span — the model process OOM'd for this sequence due to an unexpected long context. The error message in the trace is truncated sometimes by the agent; transcriptions occasionally cut long stack traces — Console stores full logs in the Request Logs view.
[03:05] Evelyn (SecOps): On the retention piece, how long do you keep request logs by default and can we push them to our S3 for longer retention for audits?
[03:14] Maya: Defaults are 30 days for hosted, but for Dedicated and Private you can set retention policies and export to your S3/GCS. We also support event streaming to your Kafka or SQS via a connector.
[03:25] Carlos: Is that export encrypted with our KMS?
[03:29] Sofia: Yes, you can supply your KMS key; for on-prem/private we also have HSM options.
[03:35] Tom: What about RBAC — can we restrict who can view request bodies vs just metadata?
[03:39] Lars: Yeah the Console has granular RBAC. You can restrict view_request_body permission separate from view_request_metadata. Audit logs capture who accessed what and we surface that in the Console under admin -> audit.
[03:51] Priya: Can you demo a debugging flow end-to-end? Like we see an error, we want to reproduce a request locally and run it through your Dedicated pool.
[03:59] Lars: Sure. Step one: from the trace, copy the request payload and headers. Step two: use our local replay tool or the "Replay" button which replays the same payload to the endpoint in a sandboxed mode.
[04:12] Lars: I'll replay the atlas-req-20270207-1142 into a canary Dedicated instance with debug logging enabled. Starting the replay...
[04:22] [04:22] (replay running, UI logs streaming)
[04:30] Lars: OK we get the same error here: stack trace shows memory allocation hit. In the trace we can see the tokenized length was 64k which is above our configured model context for the redwood-alpha-1-dev.
[04:42] Carlos: Does the runtime have safeguards around context length or do we need to block at the app layer?
[04:48] Sofia: We have configurable max_context enforcement at the routing layer, you can set soft vs hard limits. Soft limits warn and trim, hard limits reject with 4xx. We typically recommend trimming or reranking before sending extremely long prompts.
[04:59] Priya: Any way to automatically summarize/trim long contexts in-flight?
[05:04] Lars: You can plug in a preprocessor step — we provide templates and examples. Also Redwood Optimize suggests quantization and batching configs, but for trimming we suggest a light summarizer or prefix cache to reduce tokens.
[05:18] Maya: Quick aside — you mentioned auditing and compliance: we'll email the full security pack after this call.
[05:24] Priya: Thanks.
[05:30] Lars: Back to the trace, here's a span-level tag showing model_variant: redwood-alpha-1-8q, kernel: fast-attn-v2, device: p4d. That helps you map performance regressions to specific model/kernel combos.
[05:45] Tom: Is kernel selection deterministic by sequence length or dynamic?
[05:49] Sofia: It's dynamic — runtime chooses kernels based on heuristics: seq length distribution, batching, device type. We store the chosen kernel in the trace metadata so ops can correlate slowness to kernel decisions.
[06:05] [06:05] (small lag)
[06:08] Lars: Next I'll show request logs. Switch to Request Logs tab — this is raw ingestion of requests, includes headers, body (if permitted), response, and full error stacks. You can search by request id, user id, or custom header.
[06:22] Lars: For example, search for header x-atlas-user: carlos -> returns 7 requests in the window. Clicking a request opens the raw JSON payload. If bodies are redacted by policy, you'll see a redaction marker and an audit entry showing who requested unredacted view.
[06:40] Evelyn: How do you ingest logs from our side — do we push via HTTP or do you pull?
[06:46] Sofia: Both supported. For Hosted you call the Redwood API and we ingest. For Dedicated/Private you can ship logs to a configured S3, or forward via an aggregator. We also support syslog and Kafka connectors. We’ll share the ingestion schema.
[06:58] Priya: Sampling — we can't forward every single request to Redwood managed storage due to cost. What's recommended?
[07:05] Lars: We recommend 1-5% random sampling with event-based sampling for errors (100% of 5xx), and targeted sampling for VIP users or flagged flows. The Console surfaces sampling rate and shows which requests were sampled in trace vs full log.
[07:20] Carlos: Can you filter traces to show only sampled requests?
[07:23] Lars: Yep add sample:true to the filter.
[07:27] [07:27] (UI scroll)
[07:30] Sofia: One other thing — if you're running Dedicated in your VPC we can configure a push to your S3 with server-side encryption using your KMS key. For Hosted we can also configure customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest.
[07:44] Tom: For a SOC2 audit we need to show retention policy and proof of export. Is that in the admin section?
[07:51] Maya: Yes, admin -> data exports shows exports, timestamps, and you can download signed manifests for auditors. We'll include an example in the package.
[07:59] Priya: What about cross-region compliance? We need EU-only processing for some data.
[08:05] Lars: You can pin model deployments to region. Traces and logs follow the region of the deployment — for Hosted customers we also provide EU-only tenancy in eu-west regions. For Dedicated/Private you control region placement.
[08:20] [08:20] (brief pause)
[08:25] Carlos: Can Redwood correlate logs to external telemetry — e.g., link a trace to our Datadog trace id?
[08:31] Sofia: Yes, you can inject your trace id header and we include it as a tag. We also have a Datadog integration to push span metrics and events.
[08:41] Priya: Any limits on request body size for logs?
[08:45] Lars: We accept large bodies but for Hosted default max is 2MB per request body — you can configure for Dedicated. We recommend storing large artifacts in pre-signed S3 and logging pointers.
[08:58] Maya: Quick question from our side — what's your target timeline if we want to pilot Dedicated?
[09:03] Priya: Yeah timeline is T-6 weeks for security review, then we'd like a 2-week pilot.
[09:09] Maya: Ok that aligns with our playbook. We'll send SOC2 and a proposed pilot plan.
[09:15] Lars: I'll demo one more flow — error analysis aggregated view. In the Error Analysis tab we group root causes: resource OOM, tokenization errors, model inference failures, plugin/tool invocation errors. You can click a bucket to see examples and the top predicates.
[09:34] Lars: For example here's a tokenization error bucket — top offending user agents and sample payloads. You can export these to CSV for your SRE runbook.
[09:44] Tom: Do you provide auto-detection of regressions after model rollouts? We want alerts if error rates exceed baseline.
[09:50] Sofia: Yes the Console ties into Redwood Optimize — quality monitoring lets you pin a baseline and receive regression alerts by prompt set. It can auto-roll back a rollout if the error rate or quality metric degrades beyond a threshold.
[10:05] Priya: That's useful. How do you instrument canary traffic for A/B?
[10:10] Lars: Canary policy is configurable by percentage and by route. Traces will annotate which variant served the request. In the UI you can visualize success rate across variants and drift in latency distribution.
[10:22] Carlos: If a canary fails and you fallback, do you still preserve the latency and variant info?
[10:27] Lars: Yes, fallback events are recorded as spans with tags fallback:true and fallback_target: redwood-alpha-1-4q, so you can analyze how often fallback triggers and the downstream latency cost.
[10:39] [10:39] (short network blip)
[10:44] Priya: A couple of nitty gritty from SecOps — who can delete logs, and is deletion audited?
[10:50] Evelyn (SecOps): We need immutable audit trails for certain datasets.
[10:53] Lars: Deletion is gated by RBAC and recorded in audit logs. For immutable retention we recommend export to your S3 with Object Lock enabled. We'll document the recommended configuration.
[11:05] Maya: We're about 30 minutes in, do we want to run through a short checklist to capture next steps?
[11:11] Priya: Yes please.
[11:13] Maya: Action recap: Maya to send security pack and pilot proposal; Lars to share request-log ingestion docs and replay tooling; Sofia to include recommended sampling config and RBAC cookbook; Priya to circulate internal timeline and reviewers. Anything else?
[11:26] Carlos: Please also include a sample canary policy and a sample alerting rule for error-rate regressions.
[11:31] Maya: Got it.
[11:33] Priya: One more Q — any competitors we should be aware of for a feature parity check? We're also evaluating OpenAI and Anthropic plus our cloud provider's SageMaker endpoints.
[11:43] Maya: Noted; we'll include a short comparison table. In our experience Redwood focuses more on inference serving and observability than the other endpoint products.
[11:54] Tom: Quick pricing question — sample costs for Dedicated pilot vs Hosted per-token?
[11:58] Maya: We'll send a tailored quote; broadly Dedicated tends to have a committed run-rate with lower per-token cost at scale, Hosted is simpler per-token billing. I'll include a draft in the follow-up.
[12:09] [12:09] (wrapping)
[12:12] Maya: Cool — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and a proposed schedule.
[12:18] Priya: Thanks — that was helpful.
[12:21] Carlos: Thanks all.
[12:23] Maya: Bye.

End of transcript.
